A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that radiofrequency ablation and freezing of kidney tissue are both associated with a local tumour microenvironment conducive to tumour progression.

the risk of local tumour progression is higher for radiofrequency ablation than for cryoablation, and that this risk is higher in the setting of partial ablation than in the setting of complete ablation.

we have demonstrated that radiofrequency ablation and cold ablation are both effective treatments for small renal masses, but that radiofrequency ablated tumours are more likely to show incomplete ablation and to progress than cryoablated ones.
